articles.title: Shubman Gill, KL Rahul to miss final two ODIs for Test preparations; Rayudu, Karthik predict India's playing XI changes
articles.summary: India have already taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, with the third match in Hamilton abandoned due to rain.
articles.body: India have already taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, with the third match in Hamilton abandoned due to rain. With Shubman Gill and KL Rahul set to miss the final two games to prepare for the upcoming Test series, the spotlight now shifts to the batting combination Shreyas Iyer will field in the remaining matches.Former India cricketers Ambati Rayudu and Dinesh Karthik have backed Ishan Kishan and Ruturaj Gaikwad to come into the playing XI, offering India a new-look top and middle order for the final leg of the series.India take 2-0 lead after two wins, third ODI washed outIndia began the series with a five-wicket victory (DLS method) in Auckland on November 4. After bowling New Zealand out for 185 in 40.2 overs, the visitors chased down a revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli top-scored with 74 off 51 balls, while Anshul Kamboj was named Player of the Match for his two-wicket haul.The second ODI in Wellington proved to be a much tighter contest. New Zealand were dismissed for 134 in 41 overs, with Gurnoor Brar leading India's bowling effort with figures of 4/30. India were 113/7 in 26 overs when rain interrupted play, but had moved four runs ahead of the DLS par score to secure a four-run victory. Shreyas Iyer scored 30, while KL Rahul remained unbeaten on 26.The third ODI at Seddon Park in Hamilton on November 10 was abandoned without a ball being bowled due to persistent rain. India had won the toss and elected to bowl, but repeated delays and ground inspections eventually forced the officials to call off the contest.The result ensured India retained their 2-0 advantage in the series, with the final two matches scheduled to be played in Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15.Rayudu backs Ishan Kishan, Ruturaj Gaikwad for playing XIWith Gill unavailable for the remaining matches, Ishan Kishan is a strong candidate to open alongside Rohit Sharma. The left-handed wicketkeeper-batter is also the designated vice-captain for the final two ODIs, making his inclusion a likely option.Rayudu believes Kishan should replace Gill at the top, while Gaikwad should get an opportunity in the middle order in place of Rahul. He also pointed out that Gaikwad's recent role in the Indian side has not been as an opener."I would go with Ishan Kishan to replace Shubman Gill at the top and open with Rohit Sharma. Ruturaj Gaikwad has scored a 100, but he has not opened for India in recent times," Rayudu said on Cricbuzz."I think Ishan Kishan and Ruturaj Gaikwad should be coming into the playing XI, and they can be moved up and down according to what number you would like them to bat," he added.Karthik echoed Rayudu's suggestions, backing Kishan at the top and Gaikwad in the middle order. He also highlighted the left-right batting combination that the two changes could offer India."I think Ishan may be at the top, and you have played Rutu in the middle order, so he comes in for KL Rahul. You will get the left-right combination as well," Karthik said.Karthik raises question over Anshul Kamboj's replacementKarthik also discussed India's bowling options for the remaining matches, with Anshul Kamboj absent from the revised squad.He raised the possibility of giving Yash Thakur an opportunity or bringing Mohammed Siraj into the playing XI."Does Yash Thakur get a gig? Or does Mohammed Siraj come in? I hope he gets a game. So, Gill, Rahul, and Kamboj have left the playing XI, so you have three ready-made replacements in the playing XI," Karthik added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'He could be your workhorse': Ravi Shastri names this CSK pacer for New Zealand Tests
articles.summary: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri believes young pacer Anshul Kamboj could play an important role in India's upcoming two-Test series against New
articles.body: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri believes young pacer Anshul Kamboj could play an important role in India's upcoming two-Test series against New Zealand. The first Test will begin in Wellington on November 19.India have picked five fast bowlers in their 16-member squad for the series. They are Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Kamboj.Shastri feels the 25-year-old Kamboj has the qualities needed to succeed in New Zealand. He believes the Chennai Super Kings pacer can bowl long spells, keep things tight and support the other bowlers. Kamboj's batting ability is another advantage.Shastri sees Kamboj as a workhorseShastri feels India will need a bowler who can bowl long spells and hold one end during difficult periods, especially in New Zealand's windy conditions."In a country like New Zealand, in Test match cricket, you will need a workhorse, and I think he is the man who could be your workhorse - someone like a Kamboj, who can come and bowl you those 15 overs and block one end up, especially when the going gets tough, when it's very windy and things of that sort," Shastri said on the Sony Sports Network."He can bat as well. So that comes in handy for Anshul. In the middle overs in a Test match or in an ODI game, you have got to have bowlers who have the ability to take wickets. Why India is 2-0 up is because of the performance of Anshul and Gurnoor Brar. In those middle overs where India normally go to spin to pick up wickets, it's the fast bowlers who have done the job," he added."He comes across as a bloke who has done a lot of bowling in domestic cricket for Haryana and across formats. I think he will be very useful in these conditions. Sometimes you have got to pick blokes as horses for courses. He is the kind of guy who hits the bat. He is accurate," Shastri said.Kamboj impresses in ODIs after difficult Test debutKamboj's selection comes after a difficult start to his Test career. He made his debut against England but managed only one wicket while giving away 89 runs in 18 overs. He was dropped after that performance. However, the pacer has made a strong comeback on the ongoing New Zealand tour.Kamboj made his ODI debut against the West Indies on October 3, 2026. He then impressed in the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on November 4, taking 2 wickets for 22 runs. His performance earned him the Player of the Match award. He continued his good form in the second ODI in Wellington on November 7, picking up 2 wickets for 25 runs.Shastri believes Kamboj's ability to move the ball in both directions and trouble batters makes him a valuable option."More importantly, if there is something there in the surface, the ball will nibble, he hits the bat, and he can get the ball to go both ways and surprise the batter. I think a welcome addition. You have got to build your bench strength as a fast bowling unit, and I think he is one of them. For New Zealand, South Africa, and England, he becomes a good choice," Shastri said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sandpapergate row: 'Not going to answer that' - Usman Khawaja cancels media interviews after Pat Cummins question
articles.summary: Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has reportedly called off his remaining TV and radio interviews for the promotion of his autobiography, Sabr.
articles.body: Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has reportedly called off his remaining TV and radio interviews for the promotion of his autobiography, Sabr. The move follows a tough interview in which he was questioned about his claims surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as Sandpapergate.News Corp reported that publisher Penguin informed media outlets about the cancellations on Wednesday morning. This came after Khawaja faced questions from Sarah Ferguson on ABC's 7.30.Khawaja is reportedly concerned that his future interviews will focus mainly on the ball-tampering controversy rather than the other subjects covered in his book.During Tuesday's interview, he had already indicated that he did not want to discuss the allegations any further."I've talked on social media about this and I've written in my book, that's my statement, that's what it is, and I'm not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment in time," he said.Khawaja refuses to answer question about Pat CumminsDuring his conversation with Ferguson, Khawaja was asked about Warner backing his version of events and his statement that any "lies will eventually get out"."What lies is he talking about?" she asked."I'm not going to speak on behalf of Davey," Khawaja replied."I've tried my best to tell my story in an open and safe environment."Khawaja said he wanted the entire team to accept responsibility for the incident rather than leave three players to face the consequences."All I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team, and I don't think that's a lot to say. I'm not asking a lot from people and I say, 'We were a part of it. That was us'. Let's just take accountability. I was here to tell my truth, what I saw, what I felt, and to stick with those three guys who were made out to be the only people who have taken it [accountability]," he said.Ferguson also asked Khawaja whether Australia captain Pat Cummins knew about the use of sandpaper. However, the former opener did not answer the question."I'm not going to answer that."He added: "I've written what I've written in my book. I've come out and stood by those three guys and told my account of what I saw."Cummins, along with fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, had publicly denied knowing about the incident in 2021.What did Khawaja claim about Sandpapergate?Khawaja sparked a fresh debate on Saturday by claiming that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the 2018 Test against South Africa in Cape Town. His statement is different from Cricket Australia's findings at the time, which held Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft responsible for knowing about the plan before it was carried out.He also claimed that sandpaper had been used in the previous Test in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha."It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he said ahead of the release of his book.Khawaja, who retired this year after playing 88 Tests, has devoted an entire chapter of his autobiography to the scandal.What punishments did Smith, Warner and Bancroft receive?The Cape Town scandal had serious consequences for Smith, Warner and Bancroft. All three players were sent home following the incident. Smith received a 12-month ban and lost the Australia captaincy. Warner was also banned for 12 months and removed from leadership positions, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.Khawaja believes the outcome might have been different if the entire team had accepted responsibility."I don't believe the whole team would have got a ban if we went in together," he said."I think it would have been shared. It's very hard to ban the whole team."Khawaja denies making claims to boost book salesKhawaja also rejected suggestions that he had made the revelations now to attract more buyers for his autobiography.He told Ferguson that the ball-tampering issue was not part of the discussion when he signed his publishing deal in 2023. He also said his manager and publisher found out about the chapter only six months ago."Even when I gave it to them six months ago, they were shocked because I don't really talk about this to anyone," he said.The former Australia opener also explained why he chose to share his account after retiring from international cricket."The reason I felt more comfortable saying it now is because I don't speak for the team anymore," he said."If I try to come out and do it while I'm still on the team, they have to look at me every day. We have to go operate as a team."Cricket Australia responds to fresh allegationsCricket Australia has responded to Khawaja's claims and defended the findings of its investigation. However, it also accepted that the inquiry was completed within a short period."The three players who received bans after the Cape Town Test acknowledged their breaches and accepted the penalties imposed," a spokesperson told Nine newspapers."We have acknowledged that the investigation was conducted in a short timeframe given the impending Test match and that there are varying opinions about some matters including the length of the sanctions imposed. We respect that players have different recollections of events from this time."But we remain comfortable the investigation's findings accurately reflect the statements and evidence provided at the time."Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has ruled out reopening the investigation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Remember the 2025 Gautam Gambhir-Oval groundsman spat? Lee Fortis leaves Surrey after disciplinary proceedings over ECB employee altercation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lee Fortis, who worked as Surrey's head groundsman for more than a decade, has left the club after facing disciplinary proceedings over his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lee Fortis, who worked as Surrey's head groundsman for more than a decade, has left the club after facing disciplinary proceedings over his conduct.The club had sent Fortis on indefinite leave in late July after he had an argument with an England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) employee. The incident happened a day before MI London took on London Spirit in The Hundred at the Oval.Fortis also had a strong exchange with Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy, a former South Africa fast bowler, soon after the incident. He did not return to work for the rest of the summer.Fortis joined Surrey in 2012. His LinkedIn profile now shows that he left the club in October and is "open to work".A Surrey spokesperson told Telegraph Sport: "Lee Fortis has left the club and we wish him well for the future."Fortis' earlier clash with Gautam GambhirFortis had also been in the news in 2025 after an argument with India head coach Gautam Gambhir. The two had a disagreement over the Oval pitch. During the exchange, Gambhir told Fortis: "You’re just a groundsman, nothing beyond that."India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak later called Fortis "arrogant".Fortis, who is around 6ft 10in tall, was a well-known face in English cricket. He became Surrey's head groundsman in 2012 at the age of 30. His work also brought him recognition. He won the top award at the ECB's Grounds Manager of the Year Awards three years in a row, from 2022 to 2024. Surrey won the County Championship in all three seasons.What led to Fortis being placed on leave?Fortis was known for speaking directly and firmly to his staff and other people at the Oval. The incident in July was not the first time he had been involved in a disagreement.The Cricket Regulator was reported to have started an investigation into the matter. However, it did not comment when Telegraph Sport contacted it on Tuesday. The details and findings of the disciplinary proceedings have not been made public.Surrey face search for new groundsmanSurrey will now have to find someone to take Fortis's place. The search comes at an important time for the club, with the Oval set to host two major Test matches next season.The ground will stage the World Test Championship final in June, followed by the fifth Ashes Test in late July.Surrey are expected to begin looking for a replacement in the coming weeks. Gary Barwell of Warwickshire is among the names being considered for the job.The club also had a tough 2026 season. After finishing in the top two of the County Championship for four seasons in a row, Surrey found themselves fighting to stay in the division towards the end of the campaign.There was also a change in the coaching staff. Gareth Batty left his role as head coach after five years and joined Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League.Surrey are looking for a new head coach, but Rory Burns is expected to remain captain for the 2027 season. It will be his 10th year as club captain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings; Mumbai Indians get Arshdeep Singh: Blockbuster IPL trade complete
articles.summary: New Delhi: The trade between Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh was made official on Wednesday (November 11).
articles.body: New Delhi: The trade between Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh was made official on Wednesday (November 11). As part of the process, the two IPL franchises exchanged Expression of Interest (EOIs) and paperwork was submitted to the BCCI on Monday."In a marquee player trade ahead of the TATA IPL 2027, Mumbai Indians (MI) captain Hardik Pandya will move to Punjab Kings (PBKS), while Arshdeep Singh, India’s leading wicket-taker in T20 Internationals, will join the five-time champions," read IPL's official statement."Pandya will join PBKS at a fee of Rs 18 crore, up from his existing fee of Rs 16.35 crore, while Arshdeep will join MI at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore," the statement further added.Pandya is involved in an IPL trade for the second time in three years. Ahead of the 2024 season, Mumbai Indians had brought him back from Gujarat Titans in an all-cash deal and named him captain in place of Rohit Sharma — the man who led the franchise to five titles.The homecoming was meant to give MI a long-term leader and a match-winning all-rounder. In his three seasons in charge, MI finished bottom of the table in 2024, reached the playoffs in 2025, and slipped into inconsistency again in 2026. Overall, MI won just 15 of the 39 matches under his captaincy since 2024, losing 24.His win-loss ratio (0.625) for MI is the poorest for any captain to have led a team in at least 30 IPL games. It is a sharp contrast to his record with GT — 22 wins and nine defeats in 31 games. That ratio of 2.444 ranks among the best in IPL history, just behind RCB’s Rajat Patidar, who has a ratio of 2.500 from 28 matches.At PBKS, Pandya is unexpected to hold the captaincy duties which have been firmly established by Shreyas Iyer. Over the last two IPL seasons, Iyer has been the leader of the pack and it has earned him the T20I captaincy and ODI vice-captaincy. Yet, Pandya's experience could add considerable value to PBKS, who are still vying for their first-ever title, having made two finals in 19 years, in 2014 and 2025.Meanwhile for MI, after IPL 2026, MI's need for a quality new-ball partner for Jasprit Bumrah had become abundantly clear. Trent Boult had an underwhelming season and featured in only five matches. Even if MI choose to release Boult, Arshdeep Singh would give them a ready-made replacement — another bowler capable of operating across all phases, like Bumrah.It will be Arshdeep’s first IPL stint away from Punjab Kings. Since debuting for them in 2019, the left-arm seamer has taken 111 wickets in 96 matches at an economy of 9.18.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IPL 2027 trades so far: From Rishabh Pant's return to Delhi Capitals to Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh blockbuster swap
articles.summary: The IPL 2027 trading window has witnessed a flurry of high-profile player movements, with franchises reshaping their squads ahead of the December auction.
articles.body: The IPL 2027 trading window has witnessed a flurry of high-profile player movements, with franchises reshaping their squads ahead of the December auction. The latest and perhaps biggest development is the exchange involving India all-rounder Hardik Pandya and left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh, with Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings agreeing to a direct swap.Pandya will move from MI to PBKS at an increased fee of Rs 18 crore, while Arshdeep will head in the opposite direction at his existing price of Rs 18 crore. The deal adds another major twist to the build-up to the auction, following a series of significant trades involving established India internationals and overseas players.From Rishabh Pant's return to Delhi Capitals to Kuldeep Yadav's move to Lucknow Super Giants, and a four-player exchange between Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad, franchises have already made some important changes to their combinations.Here is a look at the confirmed trades so far ahead of the December auction:Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh: MI and PBKS pull off blockbuster swapThe latest headline-grabbing trade sees Pandya leave Mumbai Indians for Punjab Kings, bringing the curtain down on his second stint with the five-time champions.Pandya first joined MI in 2015 and played a key role in their title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. He returned to the franchise in 2024 and took over the captaincy from Rohit Sharma.Across 162 IPL appearances, the all-rounder has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and claimed 82 wickets. His move to PBKS comes at an increased fee of Rs 18 crore, up from his existing Rs 16.35 crore.Arshdeep, meanwhile, will join MI after eight seasons with Punjab, where he made his IPL debut in 2019. With 111 wickets in 96 matches, he is PBKS' all-time leading wicket-taker. The left-arm pacer moves at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore, giving MI an established Indian fast-bowling option.Rishabh Pant-Kuldeep Yadav: Major reshuffle between DC and LSGIn another significant exchange, Rishabh Pant will return to Delhi Capitals from Lucknow Super Giants, while left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav will move to LSG.Pant, who was bought by LSG for a record Rs 27 crore ahead of IPL 2025, will return to DC at a revised fee of Rs 15 crore. Kuldeep will join LSG at his existing fee of Rs 13.50 crore.Pant spent nine seasons with Delhi between 2016 and 2024, making 111 appearances and captaining the side in 43 matches. His two-season stint with LSG proved challenging, with the franchise finishing seventh in 2025 and at the bottom of the table in 2026.Kuldeep, meanwhile, enjoyed a successful five-season spell with DC, claiming 72 wickets in 65 matches. His move gives LSG an established Indian spin-bowling option.T Natarajan-Zeeshan Ansari: SRH welcome back experienced pacerSunrisers Hyderabad and Delhi Capitals have also completed a player exchange involving left-arm pacer T Natarajan and leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari.Natarajan will return to SRH at a revised fee of Rs 5 crore after representing the franchise between 2020 and 2024. DC had acquired him for Rs 10.75 crore at the IPL 2025 mega auction.The 35-year-old enjoyed his most successful IPL season in 2024, claiming 19 wickets to emerge as SRH's leading wicket-taker and help the team reach the final. He has 72 wickets from 73 IPL matches.Ansari, meanwhile, will join DC at his existing fee of Rs 40 lakh. The leg-spinner has taken six wickets in 10 IPL appearances, having made his debut against Delhi in 2025.CSK-SRH four-player exchange: Livingstone, Edwards head to ChennaiChennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad have completed a four-player trade involving two overseas all-rounders and two fast bowlers.England's Liam Livingstone and Australia's Jack Edwards will move to CSK, while left-arm pacer Khaleel Ahmed and Australian fast bowler Nathan Ellis will join SRH.Livingstone, who was bought by SRH for Rs 13 crore, will join Chennai at a revised fee of Rs 6 crore. Edwards moves at his existing fee of Rs 3 crore.SRH will welcome back Khaleel, who previously represented the franchise between 2018 and 2021. He joins at his existing fee of Rs 4.8 crore after taking 15 wickets for CSK in IPL 2025. His 2026 campaign was cut short by a hamstring injury.Ellis completes the exchange, joining SRH at his existing fee of Rs 2 crore. The Australian pacer missed IPL 2026 after aggravating an old hamstring injury.The deal gives CSK additional overseas all-rounding options, while SRH strengthen their pace attack with Khaleel and Ellis.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Team India splits into two groups for ODI and Test series vs New Zealand: Who went where?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Team India will split into two groups following the rain-hit third ODI against New Zealand in Hamilton.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Team India will split into two groups following the rain-hit third ODI against New Zealand in Hamilton. While one group will travel to Mount Maunganui for the remaining two ODIs, the other will head to Wellington to prepare for the upcoming Test series.India will play the fourth and fifth ODIs at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15.The two-match Test series will begin on November 19 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.The team will have a change in leadership for the final two ODIs. Shreyas Iyer will captain India after Shubman Gill led the side in the first three matches.Iyer, who is India's full-time T20I captain, is yet to lead the team in an ODI. Ishan Kishan will be his deputy for the remaining two matches.Who will join the ODI squad?Tilak Varma, Yash Thakur and Kumar Kushagra will join the Indian team for the fourth and fifth ODIs.Tilak, who was the part of the India's T20I series win 3-2 against New Zealand, last played an ODI against South Africa in December 2025. Yash and Kushagra have received their maiden ODI call-ups.The coaching team will also be split, with head coach Gautam Gambhir staying back for the fourth and fifth ODIs scheduled on November 13 and 15 at Mount Maunganui in Tauranga.Who will leave for the Test series?Shubman Gill, KL Rahul and Anshul Kamboj will not feature in the final two ODIs. They were selected only for the first three matches and will now head to Wellington to prepare for the Test series.Nitish Reddy, who was the part of the first ODI, willThe first Test will start on November 19, giving the players only a few days between the final ODI and the start of the red-ball series.The two Tests are important for India's chances of reaching the World Test Championship final. The team management will want its key players to be fresh for the series.Who will remain with the ODI squad?Shreyas Iyer, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ishan Kishan, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj and Kuldeep Yadav were part of the squad for the first three ODIs. They will remain available for selection in the final two matches.The BCCI had announced separate squads for the first three and final two ODIs to manage the workload of key players ahead of the Test series.Gill was named captain for the first three matches, while Iyer was appointed captain for the last two. articles.title: ‘If it wasn’t for the rain’: Matt Henry feels New Zealand could have pushed India in ODIs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Zealand fast bowler Matt Henry believes his side could have made the ODI series against India much closer had rain not disrupted both
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Zealand fast bowler Matt Henry believes his side could have made the ODI series against India much closer had rain not disrupted both opening matches, insisting the hosts had put up a strong fight despite trailing 0-2.India won the first two ODIs through the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method, with rain affecting the outcome on both occasions. The third ODI was completely washed out without a ball being bowled, leaving New Zealand with two more opportunities to salvage pride in the series.Henry, who is yet to feature in the contest, felt New Zealand had done well to challenge India while defending modest totals in difficult conditions."I think the way that we were defending a low total on a tricky wicket, we did really well, and if it wasn't for the rain, it was going to be a really close finish," Henry said ahead of Friday's fourth ODI."So really proud of how the guys have been going and we look forward to coming here in the Mount, which we present different challenges again. So we look forward to that and we've got two important games to come," he added.Henry set for return after concussion scareHenry is expected to return for the fourth ODI after missing the previous match due to a concussion sustained in a training-ground collision with teammate Devon Conway.The 34-year-old said he was making good progress but admitted the injury setbacks had been frustrating, particularly with a busy home summer ahead."Yeah, I've been a little bit unlucky. So thankfully, progressing well with the head," he said."It's been a bit frustrating, obviously pushing things back. But the main thing is we've still got plenty of cricket to play. And no, it's just been a really exciting summer," he added.Recalling the collision, Henry said both players had a blind spot while going through a fielding drill."Yeah, no, it wasn't ideal. We're just doing some fielding and unfortunately just both have a bit of a blind spot, so managed to have a big head clash with Dev, which was not great. So haven't seen Dev yet. He's obviously been at home, so looking forward to catching up with him and make sure he's all right as well," he said.Henry also played down concerns over a minor quadriceps issue, saying he had been cautious with the workload ahead."Yeah, no, not too concerned. That was nothing too major. It's just we've got a lot of cricket coming up. So being just smart about that. So that was fine after a couple of days," he said.Ten Tests ahead, workload management keyHenry has been named in New Zealand's 14-member squad for the two-Test series against India, beginning in Wellington on November 19. Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell are also part of the squad as they recover from their respective injuries.New Zealand are scheduled to play 10 Tests between now and March, and Henry acknowledged that managing the fast bowlers' workload would be important."At this stage, we'll get into camp. articles.title: Why Pakistan were forced to shift Sri Lanka Test from Lahore to Rawalpindi
articles.summary: Pakistan have changed the venue of the second Test against Sri Lanka because of worsening smog in Lahore.
articles.body: Pakistan have changed the venue of the second Test against Sri Lanka because of worsening smog in Lahore.The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced on Tuesday that the second match of the two-Test series will now be played in Rawalpindi instead of Lahore.Rawalpindi is already hosting the first Test of the series. The second match will also be played at the same venue from November 17 to 21. The dates have not been changed.Lahore has been facing poor air quality in recent weeks as heavy smog has covered large parts of Pakistan during the winter season.According to IQAir, a Swiss company that monitors air quality, Lahore is currently the most polluted major city in the world.The poor air quality has forced Pakistan to shift cricket matches to other venues in the past as well.In November 2020, Pakistan moved its limited-overs series against Zimbabwe from Lahore to Rawalpindi because of smog.In December 2022, a Test match between Pakistan and New Zealand was also shifted from Multan to Karachi due to similar air-quality concerns.Despite the change in venue, the second Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka will take place on the originally scheduled dates.The two teams will play the match in Rawalpindi from November 17 to 21.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joe Root: England batter does not feel ball-tampering was rife in world cricket at time of Australia 'Sandpapergate' scandal
articles.summary: Joe Root on Usman Khawaja's ball-tampering claims: "We have no idea (about it)"; Khawaja says Australia experimented with lifting seam during 2017-18 Ashes; ECB replied "no comment" when approached by Sky Sports News;  Root in England squad to face Australia in three ODIs from Friday
articles.body:
Former Baggy Greens batter Khawaja alleged in his just-released autobiography, 'Sabr', that every member of the team knew about the plot to alter the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018.

Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera applying sandpaper to the ball during a game in Cape Town and subsequently banned for nine months, with then-captain Steve Smith and David Warner , who was seen as the architect of the plot, handed year-long suspensions.

In his book, Khawaja also said Australia experimented with lifting the seam on the ball during the 2017-18 Ashes at home to England, which they won 4-0 under the captaincy of Smith.

The ECB said 'no comment' when approached by Sky Sports News.

Root, currently in Australia ahead of a three-match ODI series that begins in Perth on Friday, replied "I can only speak from my own experiences, that's not how I feel," when asked if he thought ball-tampering was rife in the sport eight years ago.

The England Test captain added of Khawaja's claims: "We obviously have no idea (about it).

"It's all speculation. I wasn't in that dressing room. I don't know what went on. I don't want to speculate, as I said. My focus is with this team right now and what we've got coming up."

Australia captain Marsh set to be grilled on Thursday

Khawaja is understood to have cancelled further promotional interviews for his book after an awkward exchange on Australian broadcaster ABC's 7.30 programme.

Australia's white-ball captain for the England series, Mitchell Marsh, played in the infamous Cape Town Test eight years ago and will surely be grilled on Khawaja's claims when he holds a press conference on Thursday.

Bowlers Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood, who issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any prior knowledge of the use of sandpaper, are not involved in the ODIs or T20s versus England.

Cummins said in South Africa ‌last month, where Australia lost 2-1 in their first Test series in the country since the 'Sandpapergate' affair, that he had spoken to Khawaja about his book and was not concerned about any potential fallout.

"He just basically gave me the heads-up that he's doing a book, and yeah, as always, no worries. Tell your story. It's fine," Cummins told reporters.

Despite Khawaja's claims, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who was not involved with the organisation at the time of the ball-tampering scandal, said there was "no compelling reason" to re-open an investigation.

articles.title: Only the second time in 149 years! Pakistan create Test history as three debutants score fifties in same innings
articles.summary: Pakistan's bold Test squad overhaul is already paying rich dividends, with three debutants scripting a rare piece of cricket history against Sri Lanka in
articles.body: Pakistan's bold Test squad overhaul is already paying rich dividends, with three debutants scripting a rare piece of cricket history against Sri Lanka in the ongoing first Test in Rawalpindi. Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha and Arafat Minhas all scored half-centuries in Pakistan's first innings, making it only the second time in Test cricket that three debutants have reached fifty in the same innings.The only previous instance came in Zimbabwe's maiden Test against India in Harare in 1992, when Andy Flower (59), Grant Flower (82) and Dave Houghton (121) achieved the feat.Pakistan handed Test debuts to four players for the contest, and all made an impact over the opening two days. While the three batters impressed with the bat, fast bowler Saqib Khan made an immediate impression with the ball, claiming two wickets to help Pakistan seize control.Pakistan declared at 434/9 on Day 2, building a substantial first-innings lead after restricting Sri Lanka to 114/3 at stumps on Day 2.Debutants power Pakistan past 400Minhas scored 52 off 72 balls, including nine fours and a six. He shared a 44-run partnership with Saud Shakeel, who narrowly missed out on a century after making 93 off 193 deliveries.Tayyab (57 off 51) and Taha (51 off 105) also contributed half-centuries to Pakistan's commanding total, underlining the impact of the new faces in the playing XI.Shakeel anchored the innings through partnerships with wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori, who made 48, and Minhas. The left-hander was dismissed in the first over after lunch, gloving a short delivery from Asitha Fernando behind the stumps. The wicket was Fernando's 100th in Test cricket.Pakistan captain Babar Azam declared at 434/9 in the second session, with Razaullah contributing a quick 17 before falling to Lahiru Kumara.Saqib strikes twice as Sri Lanka struggleSaqib carried the momentum into Pakistan's bowling innings, striking twice with the new ball. Along with experienced seamer Mohammad Abbas, he reduced Sri Lanka to 12/2, giving the hosts an early advantage.Abbas removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck, finding his outside edge, before Saqib dismissed Dinesh Chandimal with a delivery that angled across the batter and took the shoulder of his bat.Saqib later claimed the wicket of Lahiru Udara, who had scored an aggressive 42 off 47 balls with seven boundaries. Udara edged a loose drive to wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori after surviving an earlier reprieve.Sri Lanka recovered through an unbeaten 49-run partnership between Mendis and de Silva, but bad light brought an early close for the second successive day.With Pakistan's debutants dominating both departments, the hosts are firmly placed to push for a result in the Test.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the
articles.body: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the game's values during the tournament, which begins in the UAE on November 21.The award will be presented at the end of the competition on December 20, marking the first such recognition at the six-team T20 league. MCC, the guardian of cricket's Laws, will work with the tournament organisers to promote sportsmanship and fair play among players.The partnership is part of MCC's wider effort to promote the Spirit of Cricket across the game. The Club has previously worked with ICC Europe to present similar awards at three men's sub-regional World Cup qualification events earlier this year.Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations, said franchise leagues could play an important role in setting standards for player behaviour.“MCC sees franchise leagues as the standard-bearers for playing the game in the right way – playing hard but playing fair and with a smile on your face,” Lynch said.He added that the competitive nature of franchise cricket, where international team-mates often face each other, could help improve conduct across the sport.Mike Fordham, Interim Chief Operating Officer of the ILT20, said the partnership aligned with the league's emphasis on sporting values. He also pointed to the participation of players from 19 cricketing nations across its six franchises this season.“The tournament has always been hugely competitive with top quality cricket on display. Our matches have always been played in the right spirit with cricket’s traditional sporting values remaining at the forefront,” Fordham said.Season 5 will run from November 21 to December 20, with matches scheduled at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Stadium and Sharjah Cricket Stadium.Defending champions Desert Vipers will be joined by Gulf Giants, MI Emirates, Dubai Capitals, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Sharjah Warriorz in the 34-match competition. Previous winners include Gulf Giants, MI Emirates and Dubai Capitals.The new recognition will be separate from the main MCC Spirit of Cricket Award, established by MCC and the BBC in 2013 in honour of Christopher Martin-Jenkins.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Former England cricketer and match referee Chris Broad has launched a scathing attack on former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning how he could have been unaware of the incident and arguing that he escaped accountability.Broad's comments come amid fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja, who has claimed in his upcoming autobiography, Sabr, that the entire Australian squad, including players and support staff, knew about the ball-tampering episode during the tour of South Africa.Taking aim at Lehmann, who was Australia's head coach at the time, Broad questioned how he could have remained unaware of what was happening within the dressing room."Darren Lehmann surely knew all about it," Broad said on Track Radio, as quoted by Fox Sports. "And if he did not, he should not have been the coach at the time. I think he has got away lightly … OK, he left his job a few months later, but he did not get any sanctions."Broad recalls Lehmann's attack on Stuart BroadThe former England player also brought up Lehmann's criticism of his son, former England fast bowler Stuart Broad, during the 2013 Ashes series.Stuart had refused to walk after edging a delivery to the slips, prompting Lehmann to publicly criticise him. The then Australia coach subsequently warned that his side would make the England pacer "cry" when they toured Australia.Drawing a contrast with Lehmann's conduct during the 2018 scandal, Chris Broad questioned how the former coach could have denied knowledge of the incident."And here he is, the coach of the Australian cricket team that brought sandpaper out onto the field of play and denied any knowledge of this happening. I am very angry at Darren Lehmann in this respect," Broad said.Khawaja's revelations reopen Sandpapergate debateThe controversy erupted during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught attempting to alter the condition of the ball using sandpaper. Then captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner were handed one-year bans from competitive cricket, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension from international and domestic cricket.Khawaja has argued that the responsibility for the episode was collective and that Smith, Warner and Bancroft should not have been left to shoulder the blame alone. He also questioned Cricket Australia's investigation, claiming that several members of the team were not interviewed despite allegedly having knowledge of the incident.In his autobiography, Khawaja further alleged that Australia had used sandpaper during the second Test in Gqeberha, before the episode came to light in Cape Town. He also made claims about attempts to alter the ball during the 2017-18 home Ashes series, alleging that players had lifted the quarter-seam to facilitate reverse swing. Australia won the third Test in Perth by an innings, a victory that helped them regain the Ashes.Broad's criticism has also received unexpected support from former Australia opener David Warner, who was among the players handed a one-year ban following the Cape Town scandal."I could not agree more, and that's hard for me to say!" Warner wrote on X in response to Broad's comments.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rahmat Shah scripts history, becomes first Afghanistan player to enter ICC Test rankings top 10
articles.summary: Afghanistan batter Rahmat Shah has etched his name in the history books, becoming the first cricketer from the country to break into the top 10 of any
articles.body: Afghanistan batter Rahmat Shah has etched his name in the history books, becoming the first cricketer from the country to break into the top 10 of any category in the ICC Men’s Player Rankings. The 33-year-old climbed to a career-best seventh position among Test batters following a remarkable century against Zimbabwe in Sharjah.Rahmat made a significant jump of six places after producing a stunning 173 in the opening Test of the two-match series. His rise saw him move past several established international batters, including India captain Shubman Gill, South Africa’s Aiden Markram and Sri Lanka’s Kamindu Mendis.Rahmat leads Afghanistan's rise in international cricketThe 173-run knock was Rahmat's fifth Test century and his second of the year. His latest ranking position represents a career-best rating and makes him the first Afghanistan player to enter the top 10 of any category in the ICC Men’s Test Player Rankings.Afghanistan have also enjoyed success in the ODI format. Earlier this month, they reached their highest-ever position in the ICC Men’s ODI Team Rankings, climbing to sixth after winning a tri-series involving Zimbabwe and Bangladesh.Meanwhile, Zimbabwe's Craig Ervine also made significant progress in the latest Test batting rankings. The veteran batter jumped nine places to 48th after remaining unbeaten on a double-century in the second innings of the drawn Test in Sharjah.West Indies players make gains in Test rankingsThe conclusion of the ICC World Test Championship series between Bangladesh and the West Indies also resulted in notable movement in the batting rankings. West Indies batter Kavem Hodge climbed 12 places to 52nd, while Bangladesh's Towhid Hridoy broke into the top 60, reaching 60th position. Another West Indies batter, Amir Jangoo, made an impressive jump of 28 places to occupy 62nd spot.Among bowlers, West Indies spinner Jomel Warrican was rewarded for his Player of the Series performance against Bangladesh. He climbed 11 places to equal 19th in the Test bowling rankings, achieving a career-high rating. Warrican also improved his position in the all-rounders' rankings, moving up four places to 31st. His teammate Justin Greaves advanced one position to share eighth place in the Test all-rounders' list.Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh and Gurnoor Brar climb in ODI rankingsThe latest ICC rankings update also brought encouraging news for several Indian players following the opening two matches of the ODI series against New Zealand.India spinner Axar Patel gained 23 places to reach 21st among ODI bowlers after returning figures of 2/28 in the second match in Wellington. Left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh also made progress, climbing 11 places to equal 31st following his four-wicket haul in the series opener in Auckland.Gurnoor Brar registered one of the biggest jumps in the latest update. The pacer, who is currently the leading wicket-taker in the series with seven scalps, surged from outside the top 100 to 48th in the ODI bowling rankings. New Zealand seamers Jacob Duffy and Kyle Jamieson also improved their standings. Duffy moved up eight places to 43rd, while Jamieson climbed 24 positions to reach 60th.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Usman Khawaja: Former player refuses to name ball-tampering players in sandpaper scandal
articles.summary: The publisher of Usman Khawaja's autobiography denies his promotional tour has been cancelled but says there have been "adjustments" to the schedule.
articles.body:
The publisher of Usman Khawaja's autobiography has denied his promotional tour has been cancelled but says there have been "adjustments" to the schedule.

Reports in the Australian media , external said the former Australia batter had pulled out of several engagements following an interview with broadcaster ABC in which he refused to name which national team players knew of ball tampering in the 2018 Test series with South Africa.

Khawaja insisted in the interview that he wanted his former team-mates to take collective responsibility as a team, but did not want to be responsible for a "witch hunt" regarding specific players.

"The book tour is 100% still going ahead, we've just had to make some adjustments this week, but no major cancellation of the tour at all," said Khawaja's publisher Penguin in a statement to ABC.

The fall-out from the series led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft, but a Cricket Australia investigation found the national side's bowling attack were unaware of the ball-tampering.

Australia's attack in the contentious third Test - Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon and Mitchell Starc - remain fixtures in the national side.

The quartet issued a joint statement in 2021 saying they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".

Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate

How an 'absolute fluke' exposed sandpapergate scandal

Khawaja told ABC that he was simply "sharing my version of the truth" and "not calling for anything".

"It's never been for me about pointing fingers and saying, 'he did this, he said that'. That's why even when I first wrote my edit there were names, there were lots of things, and I pulled it back.

"Sometimes I'm very specific on things and sometimes they're a bit vague on things, and I do it on purpose because I'm trying to tell a story.

"My main objective here is always to try and take accountability as a team, to say, yes, this was happening. And even though one person did it or the captain knew about it and Davey Warner always took the heat for it, that it wasn't just them, that we were all involved in it as a team."

Former team-mate Warner has said the claims in Khawaja's book are "100% accurate" and that "lies will eventually get out".

Asked about Warner's comments, Khawaja said: "I'm not going to speak on behalf of Davey. I've tried my best to tell my story in an open and safe environment.

"Twenty-two pages is what sandpaper is and I've tried my best in that to explain my version of events.

"I'm not here to inflame the situation any more. I was here to tell my truth, what I saw, what I felt and to stick with those three guys that were made out to be the only people who have taken it, and I wanted that to be shown."

Pressed as to whether Cummins, who has been Australia's Test captain since 2021, knew of the ball-tampering, Khawaja said: "I'm not going to answer that."

"This has never been a witch hunt for me. It's only been those three guys who've had to cop this flak for a long time," Khawaja added.

"I'm hoping other people will come up and talk about it honestly. That's what I'm hoping, but I'm not forcing anyone to do anything.

"You've got to remember Pat Cummins is a good friend of mine, Mitchell Starc, a lot of these guys, Shaun Marsh, Mitch Marsh, they're all very good friends of mine. All I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team. I don't think that's a lot to say."

Meanwhile, England batter Joe Root said "I don't want to speculate" when asked about the scandal in the build-up to his side's first one-day international against Australia on Friday.

Questioned about the idea that ball-tampering was rife across the international game at the time, Root said: "I can only speak from my own experiences. That's not how I feel, no."

articles.title: Jacob Bethell out of England's Australia tour and doubt for South Africa Tests
articles.summary: Jacob Bethell is ruled out of England’s white-ball tour of Australia and is a huge doubt for the Test tour of South Africa following the recurrence of a knee injury.
articles.body:
Jacob Bethell has been ruled out of England's white-ball tour of Australia and is a huge doubt for the Test tour of South Africa following the recurrence of a knee injury.

Bethell has not played for England since July after suffering discomfort in his right knee while making 91 in a one-day international against India at Lord's.

He had surgery in September and looked set to return down under when he travelled to Australia for the series that begins with the first of three one-day internationals in Perth on Friday.

But the 23-year-old did not play in the warm-up match against Western Australia at the weekend and suffered what England have described as a "setback" in training earlier this week.

Bethell underwent a scan and is now set to return home to see a specialist.

England have called up Sussex all-rounder James Coles as cover, while uncapped seamer Eddie Jack has also been added to the one-day squad as a replacement for Josh Tongue, who had previously been ruled out with a toe injury.

Following the three ODIs, England play five T20s in Australia, before the Test series in South Africa begins on 17 December.

Bethell's continued absence is a huge concern for England, given the time he has already missed and his importance across all three formats.

It is also a huge blow for Bethell, whose 154 in the final Test against Australia in January was one of the few highlights of England's dismal Ashes tour. Instead of being able to build on that innings, he has been stalled by the knee injury.

The Warwickshire man was named in the squad for the three Tests in South Africa on Monday.

At the time, selector Marcus North admitted England did not know who would make way from the team that beat Pakistan 3-0 during the home summer in order to accommodate Bethell's return.

Opener Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox, batting at number three, both came into the England Test side for that series and one of them looked set to be left out of the final XI in South Africa.

Now, both Gay and Cox could be set for further opportunities to stake their long-term Test credentials.

In the summer, Ollie Pope was recalled to the Test squad as the spare batter in Bethell's absence.

Pope is due to be with England Lions in South Africa in a tour that overlaps with the Test series, so the Surrey man looks a strong contender to be promoted if Bethell is ruled out.

James Rew, who has one Test cap, and uncapped Durham opener Ben McKinney have both been in strong form on England Lions' white-ball tour of West Indies and would be other options to replace Bethell in South Africa.

Speaking before the first one-day in Australia, Test captain Joe Root told BBC Sport: "It's disappointing for Jacob. I don't know much more. I know how hard he works and everything he's done to get himself right.

"Hopefully it's not too serious and he's not out for too long."

articles.title: Jacob Bethell: England batter out of Australia white-ball tour and doubt for Test series in South Africa
articles.summary: Jacob Bethell has not played since July due to knee injury, will head back to the UK at the weekend after suffering a setback in training; left-hander could be fighting a battle to be fit for three-Test assignment in South Africa from December 17, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Batter and spin bowler Bethell has not played since scoring 91 in the final one-day international against India at Lord's in July after sustaining a right knee problem that required surgery.

The 23-year-old was hoping to return for the three ODIs against Australia, which start in Perth on Friday, and the five T20 internationals that follow, but will now head back to England after a recurrence of the injury in training and is poised to see a specialist.

Fast bowler Josh Tongue had already been already ruled out of the Australia fixtures due to a toe injury.

England have called up uncapped Hampshire seamer Eddie Jack and Sussex all-rounder James Coles into the ODI squad as replacements.

Jack and Coles were already part of the T20 party.

In Bethell's absence from the ODI side, Tom Banton has formed a successful opening partnership with Ben Duckett, so his return to the XI straightaway in that format was perhaps unlikely.

If the left-hander also misses the red-ball assignments in South Africa - live in full on Sky Sports , with the opening game at Wanderers in Johannesburg - then it will ease a selection dilemma for England.

Jordan Cox struck three half-centuries in as many matches after deputising for Bethell at No 3 in the 3-0 Test rout of Pakistan.

Should Bethell be fit to face the Proteas, there may only be space for three of him, Cox, Emilio Gay and Dan Lawrence in the XI.

Atherton: How easy will it be for Bethell to slip back in?

Sky Sports Cricket's Michael Atherton on Jacob Bethell :

"I think it is a precautionary thing given how busy the winter is but the concern is how little cricket Bethell's had and therefore how easy is it for him to slip back into the team?

"Perhaps this makes it a bit more difficult but our best wishes to him. Let's hope it is not a significant setback.

"There is a bit of Lions cricket just ahead of the main tour of South Africa. That's the good thing for him.

"There's a camp in Pietermaritzburg and four-day Test against South Africa A so there's an opportunity there once he's fit.

"If he is fit and has had game time, then I think Bethell should bat at No 3 in the Test series. If he runs out of time, he will just have to sit on the sidelines."

articles.title: 'Sandpapergate': Nasser Hussain calls Australia ball-tampering scandal 'a complete mess' after Usman Khawaja claims
articles.summary: Michael Atherton says Cricket Australia "left questions unanswered" with initial handling of incident eight years ago and that the players "not having each other's backs" will cause most "disquiet" among fans; Australia play England in eight white-ball matches from Friday
articles.body:
The 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, in which Australia's Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera trying to use sandpaper on the ball in order to make it swing, has been catapulted back into the spotlight following the release of Usman Khawaja's book.

Former Baggy Greens batter Khawaja, who played in that infamous Cape Town Test, claims the entire team knew about the scheme and not just those banned, in Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and David Warner, who was deemed the architect.

Khawaja also said he was not quizzed at the time by Cricket Australia despite sitting next to Bancroft in the Newlands dressing room and that he urged the team to come clean and take collective responsibility before being talked out of it by Smith.

Speaking on the S ky Sports Cricket Podcast , former England captain Hussain said: "I think it's a complete mess.

"Let's be honest, for the history of the game, people have been trying to work out what to do with cricket balls to make it swing more, whether it be mints, sweets, throwing the ball to the ground on the bounce, Vaseline, dirt in pocket, whatever it might be.

"[But] how a side thought it was okay to take sandpaper out, how no one before that in a meeting went, 'I don't think this is okay, I don't think we're doing the right thing', how they thought they were going to get away with it with all the cameras around [I don't know].

"Then to lie about it after and for Cricket Australia not to speak to every player, not to speak to Khawaja who was sitting next to Bancroft. It just feels like a right mess.

"The team, the baggy green, the mateship and all that stuff - that was what playing Australia was like, so for an Australian team to say, 'no, it's just those three' when it was never going to be just those three [is surprising]."

'Worst of both worlds from Cricket Australia'

Hussain's fellow analyst, Michael Atherton, is currently in Australia ahead of England's white-ball tour of the country, which begins with the first ODI in Perth on Friday (3.30am UK time).

Atherton will attend what he anticipates being a "circus" of a press conference on Thursday as Australia white-ball captain Mitchell Marsh - the only player to have figured in the Newlands Test in 2018 in the hosts' squad to tackle England - fronts up.

Usual ODI skipper Pat Cummins has been rested, along with Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, all three of whom were involved in the sandpaper Test and released a joint statement back in 2021, with spinner Nathan Lyon, denying prior knowledge of the plot.

Sky Sports pundit Atherton was critical of Cricket Australia's handling of the situation eight years ago, saying it was always "going to come back to haunt them".

Smith and Warrner were banned for a year after 'Sandpapergate' with Bancroft suspended for nine months.

Atherton, who does not see a need for a new investigation to be opened following Khawaja's claims, said: "It was almost like the sandpaper was the straw that broke the camel's back.

"It was on the back of the team having become, and Khawaja talks about it in his book, slightly out of control, a bit unlikable and with a kind of win-at-all costs mentality.

"They handed down unbelievably heavy sanctions - I thought hard-to-justify sanctions - and left three players to take the rap. But it left questions unanswered, left the door open for it to come back to haunt them, which it is doing now.

"It was eight years ago and there will be a weariness around the story eventually, because it's all over every newspaper, podcast, whatever.

"But I do think the particular point about not having people's backs is the thing causing the most disquiet [in the Australia public] and will rumble on for a while yet."

Australia have also toiled on the field, losing 2-1 in South Africa in their first Test series in the country since the ball-tampering scandal, with the out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne now dropped for the impending home clashes with New Zealand.

Amid a relentless Test calendar that then features a five-match assignment in India, the day-night 150th anniversary Test against England in Melbourne in March, and an away Ashes series in June and July, Atherton feels the Baggy Greens are in a tough spot.

He added: "The schedule is brutal and unforgiving and already there's cracks in that team.

"It doesn't feel as though the team is robust enough to get through this period.

"This [the ball-tampering claims] is adding a little bit more fuel to the fire."

articles.title: England scrap West Indies Test match with red-ball preparation ahead of Women's Ashes to take place at home
articles.summary: England's tour of West Indies in April will now comprise of three ODIs and as many T20 internationals; Women's Ashes Test at Headingley from June 24-27 will be preceded by four red-ball fixtures; four points available for winning Ashes Test in multi-format series
articles.body:
Charlotte Edwards' side were due to play cricket in the Caribbean across all three formats in April but the tour will now consist of three one-day internationals and as many T20s.

An ECB statement read that there was "insufficient time to accommodate the Test match" as part of a tour that will begin after the first round of Metro Bank One Day Cup matches, during which all England players will be involved.

Exact dates will be released by Cricket West Indies in due course.

A four-day Test at Headingley from June 24-27 kicks off next summer's Women's Ashes, followed by three T20s and three ODIs in July.

England, who have not won a home women's Test since 2005 and not secured victory in the multi-format Ashes series since 2014, will head to India in January for a 10-day red-ball training camp.

A host of multi-day matches are then scheduled for the home summer.

Plans feature a three-dayer against Australia A in the run-up to the Ashes Test in Leeds and three best-vs-best, intra-squad matches in order to build competition for places.

ECB chief executive Richard Gould said: "We are all hugely excited by the prospect of England Women taking on Australia Women in their Ashes Test at Headingley.

"It will undoubtedly be one of the highlights of the summer and is worth four points in the multi-format series, so it is important that our players have the right preparation leading into the match and are given the best chance to succeed."

Gould added: "Best versus best in English conditions provides a valuable opportunity for the team.

"It also allows us to assess our strength in depth, give opportunities to more players and get a number of competitive multi-day cricket matches across a longer period into the wider group.

"We appreciate the constructive conversations with Cricket West Indies that have enabled us to look forward to an exciting tour of the Caribbean before focusing attentions back on our home summer."

articles.title: Women's Ashes: England to prepare with red-ball matches at home
articles.summary: England cancel their scheduled Test in the West Indies in April and will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes with red-ball matches in the UK.
articles.body:
England have cancelled their scheduled Test in the West Indies in April and will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes with a number of red-ball matches in the UK.

Nat Sciver-Brunt's side have played just one Test - a heavy defeat by India at Lord's - since their last four-day meeting with Australia in January 2025, which they lost by an innings in Melbourne.

Next summer's Test against Australia, which is worth four points in the multi-format series, will be held at Headingley from 24-27 June.

England will prepare for that with four red-ball matches. One of the games will be a three-day fixture against Australia A before three intra-squad 'best v best' matches.

In addition, a dedicated red-ball training camp will be held in Bangalore in January.

England expect to use 26 or 27 players across the different training camps and matches.

It means England's schedule in the West Indies has been revised to three T20s and three one-day internationals only.

The change comes after it was suggested the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) might need to offer financial support to Cricket West Indies (CWI) to allow the Test to take place.

"We would welcome any assistance of our much wealthier member boards," CWI chief executive Chris Dehring previously told BBC Sport. "It is very expensive to host cricket in the Caribbean."

However, BBC Sport understands the ECB's decision is not related to those financial discussions and the schedule change is viewed as a performance decision in line with giving England the best chance of winning the Ashes.

West Indies have not played a women's Test since 2004, which was their only red-ball match in 47 years.

"A 10-day warm-weather red-ball camp in India followed by four further matches in English conditions will provide Charlotte Edwards and her team with the appropriate game time to be ready for that challenge [of Australia]," said ECB chief executive Richard Gould.

"Best versus best in English conditions provides a valuable opportunity for the team.

"It also allows us to assess our strength in depth, give opportunities to more players and get a number of competitive multi-day cricket matches across a longer period into the wider group."

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: England Test captain Joe Root has chosen not to comment on the fresh allegations surrounding Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: England Test captain Joe Root has chosen not to comment on the fresh allegations surrounding Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as 'Sandpapergate'.Speaking ahead of England's three-match ODI series against Australia, Root said he did not know what had happened inside the Australian dressing room and wanted to concentrate on the matches ahead."I wasn't in that [Australia] dressing room, I don't know what went on. I don't want to speculate. My focus is with this team right now and what we've got coming up," Root said. He added that England had no clear information about the latest claims and wanted to focus on the ODI series.When asked whether he had experienced similar practices in cricket, Root said, "I can only speak from my own experiences and that's not how I feel, no."Khawaja's fresh claims reopen SandpapergateThe controversy has returned to the spotlight following revelations in former Australian batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr.Khawaja claimed that ball-tampering was not limited to Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, suggesting that the wider Australian team, including support staff, knew about the practice.He also alleged that Australia had been lifting the ball's quarter seam during the 2017-18 Ashes series to help generate reverse swing. Khawaja believes the three players should not be left carrying the blame alone and has called for collective responsibility.The original scandal took place during the 2018 Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Smith and Warner received one-year bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months after being caught using sandpaper on the ball.Handscomb also avoids fresh commentsAustralian batter Peter Handscomb, who was part of the squad during the Cape Town Test, also declined to discuss Khawaja's claims."Look, I appreciate you have to ask these questions. I've had a nice day today, and it's not really something that I want to comment on right now. I'll sort of just let the powers of people do their thing,” he said.Handscomb added that players must learn to move forward despite off-field controversies and outside discussions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: David Warner starts fresh Sandpapergate row after Graeme Hick rejects Khawaja's dressing-room claims
articles.summary: The infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja, triggering a war of words between
articles.body: The infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja, triggering a war of words between former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick and David Warner. While Hick has strongly rejected Khawaja's claims that the entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper, Warner has hit back at the former coach, questioning his appointment and bringing Michael Di Venuto into the debate.What did Graeme Hick say about Khawaja's claims?Hick, who was part of Australia's coaching staff during the 2018 South Africa tour, described Khawaja's allegations as "absolutely false". He maintained that he had no knowledge of any discussions about using sandpaper and only became aware of the incident after seeing the footage on the big screen in Cape Town.Khawaja had claimed that the entire dressing room was aware of the ball-tampering, suggesting that responsibility for the incident went beyond the three players who were eventually punished.Warner responded by taking aim at Hick's appointment as Australia's batting coach, bringing former assistant coach Michael Di Venuto into the discussion.In response to an X post on the interview, Warner wrote: "Let's get the facts straight. Graeme Hick was only appointed because Cricket Australia was unwilling to pay Michael Di Venuto what he deserved. As players, we valued Michael so highly that we even offered to contribute from our own salaries to retain him. These discussions were taking place during the New Zealand tour. That alone speaks volumes about how highly we regarded him and how determined we were to keep him involved. Adds to why Graeme has spoken!!"Why has the 2018 Sandpapergate controversy resurfaced?The latest exchange follows the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, in which the Australia batter revisited the events of the 2018 South Africa tour. His account has reopened questions about how much the dressing room knew about the ball-tampering incident and whether the original investigation captured the full extent of what happened.The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018. Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball using a piece of sandpaper. The incident became known as Sandpapergate and led to major sanctions against the players involved.Warner and then Australia captain Steve Smith were handed one-year suspensions by Cricket Australia, while Bancroft received a nine-month ban. articles.title: England learn from Ashes mistakes ahead of ODIs vs Australia side engulfed by Usman Khawaja 'Sandpapergate' claims
articles.summary: England return to Perth for series-opening ODI against Australia, a year on from host of mistakes in the city setting the tone for dismal 4-1 Ashes thrashing; now it is Australia with the problems after Usman Khawaja's explosive claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa
articles.body:
The build-up to this run of white-ball matches between the Ashes rivals, which starts with the first ODI in Perth on Friday, has been dominated by Usman Khawaja's claims in his autobiography about the 2018 Australia ball-tampering scandal in South Africa.

Khawaja says every member of the Baggy Greens team back then knew in advance about the plot to alter the condition of the ball in Cape Town and that sandpaper had even been used in the previous Test of that series against the Proteas, in Gqeberha.

Mitchell Starc, one of the Australia bowlers eight years ago and still going strong now, disputes, as he always has, that he was aware of the scheme . This who-knew-what-and-who-didn't affair could rumble on for a while. There may never be a resolution.

England out to atone for last year's Ashes errors

Watching this unfold, presumably with more than a hint of glee, are England, who have returned to the scene of their own cricketing crime last winter. Not ball-tampering, of course, but a complete lack of acceptable preparation for a series as big as The Ashes.

Brendon McCullum was Test coach at that point - not now, having being sacked in July as the 4-1 Ashes debacle was followed by a 2-1 series defeat at home to his native New Zealand - and presided over a shabby lead-in to the first Test.

The sole warm-up was an intra-squad fixture on a docile deck at Lilac Hill which in no way teed the team up for the bouncy nature of the Optus Stadium surface they came up against across Perth in the Ashes opener. The result? England went down in flames.

A game they looked destined to win they ended up losing inside two days after a remarkable batting collapse induced by the unwise decision to continually drive on the up.

Even more unwise was not talking about dismissals driving on the up in between their defeat in Perth and the loss in the day-night game in Brisbane that followed.

After a pink-ball pummelling at The Gabba, the series was almost beyond them. When they retuned from a beach break in Noosa, which some observers claim was drink-laden, and they then lost in Adelaide, the series was beyond them. Ashes over.

This, though, might be a new England - with the same guy as coach in Brendon McCullum and a white-ball captain in Harry Book eager to bounce back from the chastening trip a year ago.

Michael Atherton told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast : "I think the Ashes was a bit of a wake-up call for players like Brook so he will come to this tour now a bit older and a bit wiser - and hopefully hurting to a degree where England are motivated to put on a show."

Warm-up game shows change of approach from England

The laid-back McCullum was kept on as limited-overs head coach after losing the Test job and, bar a sticky tri-series in the subcontinent when they fluffed their lines with the ball in run chases versus Pakistan and Sri Lanka, things have been going swimmingly.

Three straight bilateral 50-over series wins and also top spot in the T20 rankings, first after routing India 4-0 in July and then again by sweeping Sri Lanka 3-0 in September.

England are, in the main, making shrewd calls on the field through Brook and shrewd calls off them, too, including the choice to play a proper warm-up ahead of the Australia ODIs - last Saturday's 92-run win over Western Australia at The WACA.

That tune-up match is something that will be replicated ahead of the three-Test series in South Africa from December 17 as Joe Root's red-ball squad play a Cricket South Africa XI in Durban, while a practice game is also pencilled in when they return to Australia in March for the 150th anniversary Test in Melbourne.

On how better prepared they are for Friday's outing at the Optus than they were last November, captain Brook said: "The conditions [at the WACA] always feel a lot closer than Lilac Hill. The bounce, the carry, the pace of the pitch - it's miles away from what Lilac Hill offered us. Thankfully we got the opportunity to play there.

"The key is to try and be one of the fittest and strongest sides in the world. You can never guarantee [winning] but you can guarantee the off-field preparation can be a lot better."

Australia build-up dominated by 'Sandpapergate'

Australia's off-field preparations have surely been disrupted by Khawaja's blockbuster declarations, even if all but one of the men who played for the Baggy Greens in that Cape Town Test eight years ago are not involved in the three ODIs and five T20s.

Mitchell Marsh is the sole figure from the Newlands drama who will be around. He is captaining Australia against England and will no doubt be heavily quizzed on what he did or did not know about Cameron Bancroft's use of sandpaper on the ball.

Starc and fellow seam-bowling stalwarts (and fellow 'Sandpapergate' Test players, for that matter) Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins have been rested from the England white-ball contests - Starc has already retired from international T20s anyway.

You sense Australia will miss them in the ODIs against a strong touring team, with the pace bowling attack looking a little raw in their absence. You also sense that their names will be mentioned a lot in the wake of Khawaja's headline-making claims.

Starc, Hazlewood and Cummins, along with spin bowler Nathan Lyon, issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any prior knowledge of the ball-tampering.

Will they feel compelled to release another official one, either as a group or individually, or has all their talking been done?

What is clear is that England have a chance to make a statement in the ODIs, by proverbially kicking Australia when they are down. Down because of the 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa and down because of 'Sandpapergate' rearing its head again.

Atherton added: "When England arrived a year ago, all the guns were trained on them, the classic Pommie-bashing.

"Average Joe" Root, never got a Test hundred here. Pictures of the 'New Zealand-born, whining' Ben Stokes coming through the airport. All the usual focus on England.

"Now the focus is on the home team - and for an Englishman there is no better time to be in Australia than when the Australian team are tearing themselves apart, as they seem to be doing right now."

Schedule for England's tour of Australia

ODIs 3.30am UK time, with T20s 8.15am UK time

Second ODI: Sunday November 15 (Adelaide)

Third ODI: Wednesday November 18 (Hobart)

First T20I: Saturday November 21 (Melbourne)

Second T20I: Tuesday November 24 (Carrara)

Third T20I: Friday November 27 (Brisbane)

Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)

Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)

Former opener David Warner, who was also involved in the scandal, has supported Khawaja's claims.In his autobiography Sabr, released on Tuesday, Khawaja shared his account of the events that resulted in Cricket Australia suspending Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.When asked about the possibility of Khawaja revealing details that differed from the findings of the official investigation, Cummins had earlier said:“It’s obviously a long time ago.
