articles.title: 'I'd tape it to my thumb': Ex-Australia star admits to using sandpaper after Usman Khawaja's revelations - WATCH
articles.summary: The Sandpapergate controversy has resurfaced in Australian cricket, eight years after the 2018 scandal.
articles.body: The Sandpapergate controversy has resurfaced in Australian cricket, eight years after the 2018 scandal. Following fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his memoir, 'Sabr', ex-leg-spinner Stuart MacGill has now admitted to using sandpaper on the ball during his playing career.MacGill, who played 44 Tests and three ODIs for Australia between 1998 and 2008, said he had used sandpaper on the ball but insisted that it was not part of a bigger plan to cheat.His admission has added another twist to the Sandpapergate controversy, which took place during Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. The incident had led to bans for three Australian players and remains one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket.MacGill reveals how he used sandpaperSpeaking to former Sydney Sixers teammates Steve O'Keefe and Moises Henriques on a FanaticsTV YouTube show, MacGill explained how he would attach a small piece of sandpaper to his thumb and use it to scratch the ball."I'd cut a small piece of sandpaper and tape it to my thumb," he said. "It was not a part of a massive 'global cheating scam'; I was just really curious to see what would happen and if it would work. And oh, it works (laughs)," said MacGill.He also explained how he would use the sandpaper after tea, remove it from his thumb and throw it away before the match continued."What they would do is the umpires as you're walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there and you'd run out on the field, pick it up and go on the field. I would tape a little bit of a square of sandpaper on my thumb, pick the ball up just after tea, scratch the living daylights out of it, pull the sandpaper off, chuck it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. So nobody even knew that I'd done it, apart from all the scratches on the ball," he added.Khawaja's claims reopen SandpapergateMacGill's admission comes after Khawaja made fresh claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in his memoir, 'Sabr'.Cricket Australia has maintained that the wider Australian team was not aware of the plan to use sandpaper to change the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa.However, Khawaja's revelations have raised fresh questions about what other players knew about the incident.Darren Lehmann, who was Australia's head coach during the 2018 tour of South Africa, has strongly denied knowing about the plan to use sandpaper. Players such as Mitchell Starc have also publicly denied any involvement in the scandal.Former Australia captain David Warner, one of the three players punished over the incident, has backed Khawaja and said that the claims in his autobiography are true.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | 'Mumbai Indians were keen on Arshdeep Singh': Ness Wadia reveals how Hardik Pandya trade materialised
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia believes Hardik Pandya could bring the midas touch that the Mohali-based franchise has been missing over the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia believes Hardik Pandya could bring the midas touch that the Mohali-based franchise has been missing over the last couple of Indian Premier League (IPL) seasons. Despite showing plenty of promise over the past two seasons, Punjab Kings have fallen short of winning their maiden IPL title. Wadia feels the India all-rounder could be the missing piece in the Shreyas Iyer-led side's puzzle and help the franchise dominate the league, much like his favourite club Arsenal are doing in the English Premier League.In a freewheeling chat with TimesofIndia.com, Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia opens up about the blockbuster Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade, admitting that letting go of the India pacer was a difficult decision. Wadia explains the cricketing rationale behind acquiring Pandya, reveals how the negotiations unfolded and outlines the franchise's long-term ambitions of building a championship-winning team.ExcerptsHow long did it take for the Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade to materialise?Ness Wadia: Yes, it took a little while. I think Mumbai Indians were keen on Arshdeep, and from a cricketing perspective, we also reflected on it a lot. We believe Hardik is someone who brings a great deal to the team. Most importantly, this is not about a short-term, one-year arrangement. We are keen to build a very strong franchise that wins championships, and we feel this move will take us in that direction. We are looking at Hardik as a long-term investment, not just a short-term move.Was it always going to be a straight swap, or were other players also discussed?Ness Wadia: It was always going to be a direct swap.Arshdeep is someone Punjab Kings have invested in from a young age. He is also a local boy from Mohali and has become one of the faces of the franchise.How difficult was it to let him go?Ness Wadia: There are two ways to look at it. The way I see it, it makes me happy that he has done so well. It makes me happy that he is so much in demand. At the end of the day, it makes me exceedingly happy that he represents our country at the highest level and is one of its leaders. So, there is only happiness. That is what I have to say.What kind of conversation did you have with Hardik Pandya?Ness Wadia: We had a very good conversation with Hardik. I think he will bring a lot of experience and add tremendous value to Shreyas and Ricky (Ponting). He worked with Ricky during his initial years at Mumbai Indians and has a lot of respect for him. I think this will be a win-win situation for everyone.In the past couple of seasons, Punjab Kings have been doing well, much like the Gunners, before they went on to win the Premier League. I think we are almost there. Hardik brings that Midas touch to us.Punjab Kings were already a strong and consistent team, but Hardik's arrival seems to add something that could help the side go all the way. Was Hardik the missing piece over the last couple of seasons?Ness Wadia: No puzzle is ever perfectly complete. All the players have to come together and perform well. Timing is very important, and players go through ups and downs. But I think, as a collective group under the leadership of Shreyas and Ricky, we have proved that we can stand up and deliver.We reached the final in 2025, and were doing really well in 2026, before slipping up towards the end. I think that was down to a lack of experience. Sometimes, overconfidence also creeps in. There were also players who did not perform at their expected levels. But we certainly have the potential to win not just one, but several championships. That is the objective for Hardik, Shreyas, Ricky and all of us.You have been part of the IPL as an owner since its inception and have seen the league grow over the years. How much has the business evolved? With the introduction of the trading window, do you see the possibility of a mid-season transfer window in the future?Ness Wadia: The league has to keep evolving. I think it is good that the trading window was introduced and that it remains open even after the retention deadline. It is interesting because a lot of trades have happened this year.It shows that franchises are willing to make difficult calls, go into an auction, do the best they can and then assess how things work out over the next one or two years. They can subsequently make adjustments and tweak their squads. But as far as we are concerned, we are looking at Hardik as a long-term investment, not just a short-term move.Are there any more trades in store for Punjab Kings, or will we next see the franchise in action at the auction in Goa?Ness Wadia: You never know. Stranger things have happened! We still have few days left, so a lot can happen in that time. These things can move very quickly.Of course, if a trade is on the cards, franchises can always agree and complete it even after the retention deadline. That is the beauty of having the trading window open after retentions as well.There have been discussions and reports about extending the IPL window. What is your take on that? Do you see merit in having a longer window or shifting the tournament to a different period?Ness Wadia: As far as the IPL window is concerned, it would be good to have a different window because, with changing weather patterns, it sometimes starts raining or gets very hot, making conditions difficult for players. Ideally, one could look at shifting the tournament.However, we will have to consider the domestic and international cricket calendars and see what is possible. But it is certainly something worth exploring.How difficult is it for a franchise to play its home matches across two different venues?Ness Wadia: It is difficult. It is difficult for the players as well. But we have to look at the bigger picture. At the end of the day, it is also about the revenue we generate and the support we receive from both Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) and Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association (HPCA). It would be fantastic if that support continues. Let's see how things develop going forward. Having said that, these are world-class players, and everyone adjusts and adapts. You can look at it as having one additional venue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 4th ODI: Pacer who took 5 wickets in 5 balls added to New Zealand squad
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Zealand have added a record-breaking fast bowler Brett Randell to their squad for the remaining two ODIs against India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Zealand have added a record-breaking fast bowler Brett Randell to their squad for the remaining two ODIs against India. Randell made history earlier this year by becoming the first bowler in the 254-year history of first-class cricket to take five wickets in five balls.The 31-year-old has been included in the squad for the fourth and fifth ODIs against India. He is also in line to make his international debut in the fourth match, which will be played on Friday.India lead the five-match series 2-0 after winning the first two games. The third ODI in Hamilton was abandoned due to rain.Randell has played 145 professional matches, including five for New Zealand A. He recently returned from a stint with English county side Derbyshire in the County Championship.New Zealand Cricket has also added all-rounder Josh Clarkson to the squad for the fifth and final ODI, scheduled for Sunday.Randell's record-breaking five wickets in five ballsRandell created history while playing for Central Stags against Northern Districts in New Zealand's Plunket Shield in March this year. The 31-year-old took five wickets in five consecutive balls on the second day of the match, becoming the first bowler in the 254-year history of first-class cricket to achieve the feat.While Randell was the first to do it in first-class cricket, five wickets in five balls had been achieved in other formats before.Ireland's Curtis Campher became the first male player to take five wickets in five balls in a professional match during a domestic T20 game in July 2025.Zimbabwe Women all-rounder Kelis Ndhlovu had also achieved the feat in a domestic Under-19 T20 match in 2024.New Zealand coach backs RandellNew Zealand head coach Rob Walter congratulated Randell on his first international call-up and praised his consistent performances in domestic cricket."It's always a special time when a player earns their first international call up," said Walter."We're very pleased for Brett, he's been a consistent performer in domestic cricket for some time now and has earned this opportunity. There’s been a few movements throughout the series so we're fortunate to be able to bring in Brett and Josh," he said.Changes to New Zealand coaching staffNew Zealand Cricket has also made changes to its coaching staff as the team starts preparing for the Test series against India, which begins on November 19.Northern Districts pathway coach Mitch Renwick and strength and conditioning coach Corey Mileys have joined head coach Walter and Martin Guptill for the ODI series.Regular bowling coach Jacob Oram, batting coach Luke Ronchi and strength and conditioning coach Chris Donaldson have left the ODI squad and moved to Wellington to prepare for the Test series.New Zealand's updated ODI squadsFourth ODI: Mitchell Santner (C), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Dean Foxcroft, Mitch Hay (WK), Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Nick Kelly, Brett Randell, Tim Seifert (WK), Will Young.Fifth ODI: Mitchell Santner (C), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Kristian Clarke, Josh Clarkson, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Dean Foxcroft, Mitch Hay (WK), Nick Kelly, Brett Randell, Tim Seifert (WK), Blair Tickner, Will Young.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ball-tampering row: Pat Cummins invites media, to address 'long list and full extent' of Usman Khawaja's allegations
articles.summary: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins is set to respond to Usman Khawaja's allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying he needed time to
articles.body: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins is set to respond to Usman Khawaja's allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying he needed time to understand the claims made in the former opener's autobiography before addressing them.Khawaja's book, 'Sabr', released on Tuesday, has brought the controversy surrounding the Cape Town Test against South Africa in 2018 back into focus. In the book, Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball.He also alleged that then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft were made scapegoats by cricket administrators despite other members of the team allegedly knowing about the plan.Cummins said he would address the media on Friday at Cricket Central, where he is scheduled to train ahead of New South Wales' Sheffield Shield match."I'm training at Cricket Central tomorrow morning before the Blues play in the Shield match," Cummins wrote on 'X'."Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30 am. I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly."Khawaja, meanwhile, has withdrawn from interviews to promote his autobiography after facing criticism over his television interview on Tuesday evening. During the interview, he struggled to address questions about the allegations, including whether Australia's four frontline bowlers, Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, were involved in discussions about ball-tampering.He was also directly asked whether Cummins knew about the plan to use sandpaper in advance. Khawaja declined to answer, saying he had only shared his "truth" in the book.Former Australia captain Michael Clarke has also questioned Cummins' silence on the matter, saying the team needs to establish what happened during the 2018 Test.Speaking on 2DayFM's Breakfast with Nath & Emma, Clarke expressed surprise that the current Australia captain had not yet addressed the allegations publicly."I can't believe we haven't heard from Pat Cummins yet, the Australian captain," Clarke said.Clarke also pointed to the impact of the 2018 scandal on Australian cricket's leadership, suggesting that Cummins might not have become captain had Smith not been removed from the role following the incident.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 21 sixes in an innings! New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs comes close to world record
articles.summary: New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs produced a stunning batting display in the domestic Ford Trophy on Thursday, smashing an unbeaten 202 off just 137 balls
articles.body: New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs produced a stunning batting display in the domestic Ford Trophy on Thursday, smashing an unbeaten 202 off just 137 balls against Otago in Auckland.The 21 sixes in his innings set a new record for the most sixes hit by a New Zealand batter in a List A innings. Jacobs was just two sixes short of the world record of 23, held by Australia's Da’Arcy Short.His powerful knock helped Auckland post 334/8 at the Kennards Hire Community Oval. However, Jacobs' effort went in vain as Otago chased down the target in 49.1 overs.A total of 34 sixes were hit in the match.Jacobs hits 21 sixes in record-breaking knockBatting at No. 4, Jacobs turned his maiden List A century into a double century with some powerful hitting. He reached the 200-run mark in just 137 balls, hitting seven fours and 21 sixes.The 21 sixes are the most by a New Zealand batter in a List A innings. Jacobs came close to breaking the world record, which belongs to Australia's Da’Arcy Short. Short had hit 23 sixes while scoring 257 off 148 balls for Western Australia against Queensland in Sydney in 2018.Jacobs also became only the fourth New Zealand batter to score a double century in List A cricket. He joined Jamie How (2012), Martin Guptill (2015) and Chad Bowes (2024) on the list.His 202 not out was also a record score for Auckland Aces in the Ford Trophy and the third double century in the tournament's history.From India series to domestic recordJacobs recently featured in New Zealand's five-match T20I series against India. He scored more than 135 runs against the world champions and followed it up with this remarkable performance in domestic cricket.The 28-year-old has also played 16 T20Is for New Zealand since making his debut in late 2024. However, he is yet to make his debut in ODIs and Test cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Sandpapergate': Australia captain Pat Cummins to address Usman Khawaja claims on Friday
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja says in new book 'Sabr' that every Australia player was aware of ball-tampering scheme in Cape Town in 2018; current Test captain Pat Cummins confirms he's "happy to speak with any and all media" on Friday; white-ball skipper for England series Mitch Marsh declined to comment
articles.body:
Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', bringing the scandal back onto the agenda after eight years.

Cummins has been rested for the white-ball series' against England, which also begins on Friday with the first ODI in Perth, but has publicly invited a media grilling in Sydney for that same morning.

"I'm training at Cricket Central (in Sydney) tomorrow morning before the Blues play in the Shield match," Cummins posted on X on Thursday. "Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30 am.

"I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly."

In the immediate aftermath of the Cape Town Test in 2018, in which Cameron Bancroft was caught using sandpaper on the ball, only he, then captain Steve Smith and David Warner - who said on Monday that Khawaja's version of events was "100 per cent accurate" - were banned.

Khawaja's revelations have invited renewed speculation over the role of the bowling group who benefitted from the ball manipulation - with Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon having previously distanced themselves from the episode.

In 2021, the quartet issued a carefully worded statement responding to "rumour mongering and innuendo" in which they denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball in order to try and make it swing.

Cricket Australia chairman David Boon has backed Cummins, saying his job as skipper is not under threat.

"We absolutely support Pat," Boon said in comments published by The Australian on Thursday. "He's been an exemplary captain, he's led the team ​with integrity and, you know, very successfully over the period of time that he's been captain, so there's no question of our confidence in him continuing on in that fact."

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, after Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg insisted there would be no re-opening of the 'Sandpapergate' investigation , Starc said of Khawaja's claims: "I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair.

"There are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process, at the time and since.

"I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers but from where I stand my opinion hasn't changed, my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021.

"As far as our statement said, we weren't aware of things being taken on the field. That's where I'll leave it.

"I will be sticking to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time eight years ago, so clearly there are differing versions from different people.

"We weren't aware of anything taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town.

"As far as the book is concerned, I haven't read it. I probably won't read it, so that's for Usman to elaborate on."

On Khawaja saying the ball was also tampered with in the Test before the Cape Town fixture, at Port Elizabeth, now Gqeberha, Starc added: "That's the first I was aware of any of that."

Starc, Cummins, Hazlewood and Lyon are not part of the upcoming white-ball series at home to England.

Marsh not drawn on Khawaja claims | Root: It's all speculation

Captain of Australia for the three-match ODI series and five T20s against England, Mitchell Marsh - who was in the Test team that toured South Africa in 2018 - declined to comment at a press conference in Perth on Thursday.

"I respect (Khawaja) for telling his story and for writing his book, and I don't sit here coming from a place of judgment on any of that," Marsh said ahead of Friday's series-opening ODI.

"It was a really tough time for Australian cricket. There's still a lot of people hurting. Now is not the time for me to share my story.

"My honest answer is because I've personally moved on. I respect that others probably haven't, but I have. And I hope that's respected."

He added: "Everyone's got their story. Some will be willing to share it, and others might not, purely on the basis of the fact that they've moved on. I think it's really important that at some stage we do."

In his book, Khawaja also said Australia experimented with lifting the seam on the ball during the 2017-18 Ashes at home to England, which they won 4-0 under the captaincy of Smith.

The ECB said 'no comment' when approached by Sky Sports News .

"It's all speculation. I wasn't in that dressing room. I don't know what went on. I don't want to speculate, as I said. My focus is with this (ODI) team right now and what we've got coming up."

Cricket Australia: No compelling reason to re-open 'Sandpapergate' case

A statement from the Australian Cricketers' Association called the 2018 scandal a "low point for Australian cricket" for which Smith, Warner and Bancroft paid an "enormous" and "disproportionate" price.

The statement added: "There are no winners in this issue, and nothing can undo what happened. There are humans in the centre of this and we will be calling for the ongoing vitriol directed at those involved to come to an end."

Greenberg, who was not part of Cricket Australia at the time of the scandal, told Australian radio station SEN on the decision not to launch a fresh inquiry: "We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again.

"I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman. Our position hasn't changed on that.

"There's absolutely no benefit in going back, that's the clear position of the CA board. I think it's fine, we've got to look ahead, and the matter was dealt with under a previous leadership back in 2018.

"Trying to second-guess decisions from a previous time or making an assessment through the prism of hindsight is not something we want to do."

'Usman's version of events inconsistent with what others say'

The Cricket Australia CEO added: "When you cut to the core of the challenge that we face here, Usman's version of events is inconsistent with what others have had to say.

"I can assure you there are lots of other players who have a very, very different version of events and they have made that very public from the very start of 2018.

"They have been very consistent in their position right through until today. From my conversations with many over the weekend, I don't think that will change either.

"I think we end up at the same intersection point, which is that eight years ago people have a version of events which differ from each other.

"No one would like to get this chapter of Australian cricket closed more than me, but it is unlikely."

Former Australia captain Michael Clarke hopes the truth comes to light, saying that chance was missed in the wake of the scandal in 2018 and then again three years later when Bancroft replied it was "probably self-explanatory" after being asked whether the bowling attack knew of the sandpaper use.

Clarke told 2DayFM : "[Australia fans] can't trust what's real. They don't know the truth until this gets reopened and the truth comes out. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to move on.

"For me, right now, there are more questions than answers. I want to know, firstly, did everyone know? Because certain players have come out and said they didn't. That's important information so we can get the truth.

"I can't believe we haven't heard from Cummins yet. Steve Smith lost his job. If this doesn't happen, Tim Paine never captains Australia. And neither does Cummins.

"Cummins would not have captained a game at this stage if 'Sandpapergate' didn't happen because Smith would still be captain."

articles.title: Australia sandpapergate scandal: Mitchell Marsh dodges Usman Khawaja claims as Pat Cummins vows to speak
articles.summary: Mitchell Marsh persistently refuses to speak about Australia's ball-tampering saga at a press conference but captain Pat Cummins vows to "respond properly".
articles.body:
Mitchell Marsh persistently refused to speak about Australia's ball-tampering saga at a news conference on Thursday but captain Pat Cummins said he will "respond properly" later.

All-rounder Marsh, 35, was Australia's bowler when the scandal first came to light in the 2018 Cape Town Test and is standing in for Cummins as 50-over captain for the series against England, which starts on Friday.

But, pressed for his view on 'sandpapergate' after it was brought back into the spotlight by Usman Khawaja's autobiography , he repeatedly said "I'm not here to go back on my recollections of South Africa".

"This is my choice not to go back there," he said. "Who knows maybe I will write a book one day."

It came after Cummins and Cricket Australia announced an impromptu news conference for Friday morning (22:30 Thursday GMT).

"Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week," Cummins said on social media.

"I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly."

While Cummins was backed to remain as captain by Cricket Australia's interim chair David Boon on Thursday, he is yet to speak since Khawaja's book was released.

"We absolutely support Pat," former batter Boon told newspaper The Australian.

"He's been an exemplary captain, he's led the team with integrity and very successfully over the period of time that he's been captain, so there's no question of our confidence in him continuing on in that fact."

Since the release of Khawaja's book, much of the discussion has surrounded whether Cummins and the other bowlers - Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, who all remain part of the team - were aware of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball.

In 2021, the quartet released a joint statement which said they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".

Writing in his book, Khawaja said "it was all of us" and called for the players to take collective responsibility. He said there had been a discussion about using sandpaper to rough up the ball and promote reverse swing during the previous Test.

The topic has overshadowed the build-up to the three-match one-day international series between Australia and England, which begins at 03:30 GMT on Friday.

England captain Harry Brook said he "hasn't seen any" of the debate.

"Obviously I have heard some conversations but we weren't in that dressing room, we have no idea what happened, we are out here now and have a good challenge against Australia," Brook said.

"We are just trying to focus on ourselves."

Marsh added: "There's been a lot of noise around this week and I respect that certain people have told their stories, but I'm not here to share mine today.

"I know that might sound weird, but it's a big week for us and an important time for this one-day group, and my sole focus has been on preparing for tomorrow."

Asked why he did not want to share further details, he said: "My honest answer is because I've moved on, I respect that others probably haven't, but I have. And I hope that's respected."

articles.title: James Anderson signs for Surrey: Former Lancashire and England great to continue career at age of 44 in County Championship
articles.summary: James Anderson was released by Lancashire after 2026 season, despite taking 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 as they finished second-bottom of Division Two; Surrey won three consecutive County Championship titles from 2022 to 2024; runners-up in 2025, they finished seventh last season
articles.body:
Anderson, England's all-time leading wicket taker, was released by boyhood club Lancashire in October after over 25 years with the county, a decision he said left him "sad" and "quite shocked" and made him question if there was something "fundamentally wrong with me as a person".

Upon the announcement of his move to the Kia Oval, Anderson said: "It's an honour to join a club like Surrey and I can't wait to start a new chapter in my career.

"I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games of cricket.

"I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country."

Anderson, who turns 45 in July of next year, will get the opportunity to add to his haul of 1,193 first-class wickets and perhaps more silverware to a glittering CV that includes four Ashes series victories and the 2010 T20 World Cup in the Caribbean.

The Burnley-born bowler picked up 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 in County Championship Division Two for Lancashire in 2026.

His exit from Old Trafford came as the hierarchy, including new director of cricket Paul Farbrace, plot to build an attack for the future after a poor few seasons in red-ball cricket.

Anderson captained Lancashire last term as the county finished second bottom of the second tier, ahead of only Gloucestershire.

Surrey have won the County Championship on 22 occasions, including three in a row from 2022 to 2024. They were runners-up in 2025 but had a disappointing 2026 campaign in which they finished seventh.

Surrey's director of men's cricket, Alec Stewart, said: "We're delighted to bring someone of the calibre of Sir James Anderson to Surrey.

"Jimmy brings quality with the ball. His 50 championship wickets last season prove that he is still one of the best bowlers in the country.

"Jimmy also brings a wealth of experience to the group that all our bowlers will learn from. Much of our squad have international aspirations, and they will learn a great deal from training, playing and being in the same dressing room with Jimmy."

Anderson - who is poised to play in the Italia T10 for Napoli Knights later this month - was forced into international retirement by England in 2024.

He took four wickets in his final Test, against West Indies at Lord's, to end with 704 wickets across 188 games in the longest format, at an average of 26.45.

He is the most prolific pace bowler in Test history, with only Sri Lankan off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan (800) and Australian leg-spinner Shane Warne (708) taking more wickets.

May 2002 - Anderson makes first-class debut for Lancashire; takes his maiden first-class wicket in May, dismissing Ian Ward.

December 15, 2002 - Anderson makes ODI debut for England against Australia in Melbourne, aged 20.

February-March 2003 - Anderson selected in England's squad for 2003 Cricket World Cup, producing match-winning spell against Pakistan. England lose to eventual champions Australia.

May 2003 - Anderson becomes youngest player to take a hat-trick in Lancashire history - the first at Old Trafford for eight years.

May 22, 2003 - Anderson makes Test match debut for England against Zimbabwe at Lord's, still aged 20. Takes five wickets in an innings on debut.

August 2003 - Anderson unanimously voted as England's Young Cricketer of the Year.

September 2003 - Anderson handed central contract with the ECB.

July 2005 - After period out of the England squad, Anderson is recalled for final Test of Ashes series, but fails to make team.

September-December 2006 - After a back stress fracture and six months out, Anderson returns to England side for Ashes series in 5-0 whitewash defeat in late 2006.

January 2007 - Anderson plays in his first T20 International, playing for England against Australia in Sydney.

2009 - Anderson is named one of five Wisden Cricketers of the Year following a standout Test series against in 2009 Ashes victory.

September 2011 - Anderson helps Lancashire win the County Championship title.

July 2014 - Batting at No 11, Anderson makes 81 against India, his highest Test total

March 2015 - Anderson plays his final ODI match for England against Afghanistan in Sydney.

April 2015 - Against West Indies, Anderson becomes England's record Test wicket-taker with his 384th dismissal.

July 25, 2016 - Anderson becomes first fast bowler to take 50 wickets against all other seven major Test-playing nations, Australia, India, New Zealand, Pakistan, South Africa, Sri Lanka and West Indies.

December 26, 2019 - Anderson becomes ninth cricketer to play in 150 Test matches.

January 5, 2020 - Anderson takes 28th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, overtaking Ian Botham's England record.

March 9, 2024 - Anderson becomes only third player in history to reach 700 career Test wickets

July 2024 - Anderson announces international retirement having played his 188th and final Test match for England against the West Indies at Lord's.

April 2025 - Knighthood | Appointed a Knight Bachelor in recognition of his services to cricket.

2025-2026 - Lancashire Captaincy & Contract. Returned briefly to T20 cricket, signed a one-year extension, and was named Lancashire red-ball captain for the 2026 County Championship season.

October 2026 - Anderson leaves Lancashire after contract not renewed

November 2026 - Joins Surrey ahead of 2027 County Championship season

articles.title: James Anderson, 44, signs for Surrey after Lancashire exit
articles.summary: Legendary England bowler James Anderson extends his record-breaking career beyond his 45th birthday by signing for Surrey.
articles.body:
Legendary England bowler James Anderson has extended his record-breaking career beyond his 45th birthday by signing for Surrey.

England's all-time leading Test wicket-taker was not offered a new contract by Lancashire, the county for whom he first played professionally 25 years ago.

Amid interest from multiple clubs, the 44-year-old has agreed a move to The Oval.

Surrey have said the deal is for the 2027 season, but it is understood Anderson could play on beyond next year.

"Going from thinking I might not play cricket again to having this opportunity - I'm properly buzzing for it," he said on a special episode of his Tailenders podcast.

"I'm just incredibly excited. I'm not doing this for a send-off. That's not the reason I've signed for Surrey."

Referring to his exit from Lancashire last month, Anderson said: "There was a bit of emotion in that few days.

"I was really conscious on not making a decision based on that emotion, so that's why I have taken a few weeks to try to get my ahead around everything and decide what the best way forward is.

"Finding a club that wants me and has that same motivation to win trophies - I just want to be a part of something."

Listen: Anderson explains Surrey move on Tailenders podcast

The move to Surrey is another – probably final – chapter in Anderson's remarkable career.

After taking 704 wickets in 188 matches, Anderson, who turns 45 in July, sits third on the all-time list of Test bowlers, with more scalps than any other seamer.

His 991 international wickets is also an England record and a record for all pace bowlers.

Anderson was forced into international retirement by England in the summer of 2024, then returned to play for Lancashire for two seasons, captaining them this summer.

Although Anderson claimed 50 wickets, Lancashire finished second bottom of Division Two of the County Championship.

New Lancashire director of cricket Paul Farbrace took the decision to release Anderson as part of a "rebuild" of the squad.

In leaving Old Trafford, Anderson has departed a ground which has an end named after him.

Now Anderson links up with Surrey after talks with director of cricket Alec Stewart, who was in the England team when the seamer made his international debut in 2002.

Anderson has signed a red-ball only deal, although Anderson he said he would play white-ball cricket if required. There is no official coaching element to the contract.

Anderson has not decided if he will relocate his family – his wife and two daughters – from their home in Cheshire.

"After thinking what would be best for me, what's best for my family and where I want to play, it was a fairly easy decision," said Anderson.

"I did feel like I wanted to play again after having a good year last year. I don't feel like I'm done yet. I feel like I've got more to offer on the field.

"Surrey is such a strong squad, challenging for the Championship. It's the chance to play in Division One again, which I haven't done for a few years. I just thought it was a really exciting challenge to try to take on.

"Weighing up all the factors, this just felt like the best fit. It's a really strong squad: past internationals, present internationals, future internationals. I just thought it would be an exciting challenge."

Surrey won the County Championship in 2022, 2023 and 2024. After finishing second in 2025, they struggled in 2026, briefly flirting with relegation.

The addition of Anderson boosts a seam attack that was often hit with injuries this summer.

Anderson also adds depth given Surrey have three pace bowlers centrally contracted by England.

Gus Atkinson has been joined on the England contract list by Matthew Fisher, while Henry Crocombe, a winter arrival from Sussex, has just been awarded a two-year deal with the national team.

"I don't know how much I'm going to play," said Anderson. "It's a strong squad and there are a lot of quality bowlers in that group. I'm just trying to add some quality to that group and help out off the field if I can.

"The last couple of years at Lancs, I've worked really hard on my fitness, making sure I can play a number of games. Last year I played more than I thought I would.

"All I can do is make sure I'm bowling as well as I can, I'm as fit as I can be, and try to help out when they need me."

Beyond Anderson's arrival, Surrey are also looking for a new head coach following Gareth Batty's decision to join the staff at Indian Premier League side Chennai Super Kings.

Analysis: Imagine an Anderson farewell at The Oval

When news of Anderson's abrupt exit from Lancashire emerged there were plenty who thought, quite reasonably, that it would mean the end of his storied career.

But Anderson had intended to play on for at least one more season at Old Trafford.

Instantly, other counties expressed an interest. Realistically, none would be able to compete with the lure of Surrey.

Anderson's move to The Oval makes sense for all involved. Whereas he shouldered the burden of Lancashire's attack, he can plug in and out of Surrey's team as and when required. He could be the addition that pushes them towards another title.

Although a move south represents some upheaval in Anderson's personal life, he will be in familiar surroundings in London, not least because of his great friends from the Tailenders podcast.

Somewhat romantically, a new county also puts the conclusion of Anderson's career back in his own control.

He was denied the chance to end his time as an England player on his own terms and, when history repeated itself at Lancashire, Anderson even wondered if it was because of his character.

Now he finds himself playing at a home ground synonymous with goodbyes, where so many greats of the game have taken their last bow, while Surrey attract comfortably the biggest crowds in county cricket.

Imagine a scenario when Anderson finally call it quits and the stars align for a farewell appearance in front of a full house at The Oval. It will be absolutely rocking.

articles.summary: Shreyas Iyer will lead India for the first time in ODIs when they take on New Zealand in the fourth match of the five-match series at Bay Oval in Mount
articles.body: Shreyas Iyer will lead India for the first time in ODIs when they take on New Zealand in the fourth match of the five-match series at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday. The Indian batter will also have a point to prove with the bat after his struggles against the short ball resurfaced during the series.India lead 2-0 in the series and will look to seal it with a win in the remaining two matches. articles.title: ‘It could well be KL Rahul’: Ex-India cricketer on Delhi Capitals captaincy plans after Rishabh Pant trade
articles.summary: Former India cricketer and commentator Aakash Chopra has flagged several concerns surrounding Delhi Capitals' preparations for the upcoming IPL season
articles.body: Former India cricketer and commentator Aakash Chopra has flagged several concerns surrounding Delhi Capitals' preparations for the upcoming IPL season following their trade for Rishabh Pant from Lucknow Super Giants. While the franchise has strengthened its batting options, Chopra believes uncertainty over the captaincy and questions surrounding the pace-bowling department could pose significant challenges.The biggest question, according to Chopra, is who will lead Delhi. With Pant and KL Rahul among the potential candidates, the franchise still appears to have a decision to make. Chopra also suggested that Axar Patel may not be keen on taking up the leadership role, making Rahul a possible frontrunner.“There are multiple questions, actually. It’s an MCQ because who will be the captain? Rishabh Pant has been a captaincy candidate, KL Rahul is an option, and I’m hearing that Axar doesn’t want to be the captain. So, with everything going on, you don’t even know who will captain the side. It could well be KL Rahul at this stage,” Chopra told JioStar.Chopra also underlined the importance of getting Pant's batting position right. Having brought the wicketkeeper-batter back through a trade, Delhi must ensure that he gets an opportunity in the top four rather than being pushed down the order. He felt that failing to do so would prevent the franchise from making full use of Pant's abilities. Chopra also believed Lucknow may have come out better from the exchange, given the quality of bowler they received in Kuldeep Yadav.“And Rishabh Pant, now that you have traded him, must bat in the top four. If you are going to bat him lower than that, then you will not utilise him to his fullest potential. I felt that in that trade, LSG was better off because you couldn’t have asked for more than a bowler of Kuldeep’s calibre for that pitch,” he added.While Delhi have assembled a formidable batting lineup, Chopra feels their bowling resources could be a major area of concern. The uncertainty surrounding Mitchell Starc's availability is one of the factors, with the franchise potentially having to reassess its pace-bowling combinations depending on the Australian's participation.He also questioned the returns expected from Delhi's more expensive fast-bowling options, pointing out that Mukesh Kumar and Auqib Nabi command substantial investments, while Starc comes at an even higher price. In contrast, Lungi Ngidi proved to be an excellent bargain after being acquired for Rs 2 crore. Chopra also mentioned Dushmantha Chameera and Kyle Jamieson as relatively economical options.“Ashutosh, Sameer Rizvi, Tristan Stubbs, plus Axar Patel, and then you’ve got Miller. So, it’s a very decent setup. The problem area for them will be their bowling department. Because Mitchell Starc, will he play? It will be a conversation as to whether he will be available to play or not. They will face an issue with their fast bowling this season and how they plan to address it, I’ve got no idea.“Mukesh is at eight crore, Auqib Nabi at Rs 8.4 crore, and then you have Mitchell Starc at nearly 12, so that’s a lot of money. Lungi Ngidi was cheap, picked up for Rs 2 crore. He turned out to be a fantastic bargain. Dushmantha Chameera and Kyle Jamieson weren’t as expensive either. But the more expensive players might not be available. Their pedigree and current form are still uncertain, and Mukesh Kumar’s T20 numbers have actually plummeted a little,” Chopra stated.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
